slides.headline: Coral Castle holds more than 1,100 short tons
slides.body: Edward Leedskalnin quarried and sculpted more than 1,100 short tons of oolite limestone into Coral Castle.

photo.query: Coral Castle Florida carved oolite limestone structures
photo.prompt: wide photo of Coral Castle's carved limestone structures and walls near Homestead, Florida, no people

slides.headline: That work took more than 28 years
slides.body: Leedskalnin spent more than 28 years building it and refused to let visitors watch him work.

photo.query: Coral Castle pulleys simple tools limestone blocks
photo.prompt: nighttime photo of limestone blocks, pulleys and simple tools at Coral Castle, no people

slides.headline: And he started it after a rejected wedding
slides.body: Coral Castle material says his 16-year-old fiancée rejected him in Latvia one day before their wedding.

photo.prompt: archival portrait of Edward Leedskalnin beside carved limestone at Coral Castle

slides.headline: Which began as Ed’s Place in Florida City
slides.body: Around 1923, he built the first version at 18900 SW 352nd Street in Florida City and named it Ed’s Place.

photo.prompt: historic photo of a remote 1920s Florida City road near the Everglades with limestone blocks and scrubland

slides.headline: Then he moved it 10 miles north
slides.body: Around 1936, he moved the castle 10 miles north to its current location near Homestead.

photo.query: Coral Castle entrance South Dixie Highway Florida
photo.prompt: roadside photo of the Coral Castle entrance on South Dixie Highway near Homestead, Florida, no people

slides.headline: So visitors paid 10 cents, then 25 cents
slides.body: In Florida City, tours cost 10 cents. After the move, he asked for 25-cent donations and let people in free if they had no money.

photo.query: Coral Castle Rock Gate entrance signs Ring Bell Twice
photo.prompt: close-up photo of Coral Castle's carved rock entrance sign reading Ring Bell Twice, no people

caption:
